title: Extract shared logic
why: The same normalized code block appears in more than one location.
suggestion: Extract shared logic or raise min_duplication_lines if the duplication is intentional.
limitations: At most 32 deterministic locations are retained per fingerprint.
Predominantly literal data tables and non-alphanumeric visual data are excluded.
Block-comment and HTML-comment license headers are excluded.
Python and shell hash-comment license headers are excluded.
SQL migration and archive history is excluded from duplication comparison.
Mutually exclusive single-tag Go build flavors are excluded.
Dart constructors composed only of field- and super-formal parameter forwarding are excluded.
Rust multiline string content is excluded from code-duplication windows.
Rust trait implementations made entirely of required receiver-forwarding boilerplate are excluded.
Standalone Python triple-quoted documentation strings are excluded from code-duplication windows.
Standalone scaffold template roots are compared independently because they cannot share runtime code.
Localization implementations are compared independently because parallel translations cannot share runtime code.
Python function and annotation-only declarations are excluded from duplication windows; executable bodies remain comparable.
Mechanical shell-completion dispatch is excluded because repeated branches are derived from command schemas.
Ambient TypeScript declaration modules (.d.ts, .d.mts and .d.cts) are API contracts, not executable implementations, and are excluded.
Rust spans composed entirely of imports, attributes, data-type declarations and function signatures are excluded; executable bodies remain comparable.
Rust enum-pattern lists mapping only to literal values are static membership data and are excluded; computed match-arm bodies remain comparable.
Ordinary TypeScript source and callback bodies remain comparable; lexical equality does not prove that extraction is architecturally appropriate.
